references.text: The Lord will let the plague cling to you until he has destroyed you from the land you are entering to take possession of it. Both verses speak of the Lord's plagues and diseases as punishment.
The Lord will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, scabs, and itching that cannot be healed. Both verses describe serious diseases as God's judgment.
The Lord will strike you with painful sores on your knees and thighs that cannot be healed. Both verses speak of incurable plagues from the Lord.
The Lord will keep all sickness away from you. None of the evil Egyptian diseases you know about will he lay upon you. The contrast between blessing and curse regarding disease.
None of the diseases I placed on the Egyptians will I place on you if you listen to the voice of the Lord. Both texts mention Egyptian plagues and diseases as possible punishment.
God sends plagues that are unique and wondrous. Same theme about God's extraordinary plagues.
Isaiah describes Israel's sickness and wounds as a result of sin. Thematic parallel about plagues and disease as a consequence of disobedience.
